hints.content:
Usually, there are many different ways to divide polynomials. Here, we will use the method of splitting the quotient into multiple quotients:

$\dfrac{5x^2+x+7}{x}=\dfrac{5x^2}{x}+\dfrac{x}{x}+\dfrac{7}{x}$

Now let's try to cancel common factors in the resulting terms.

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{5x^2}{x}&=5x
\\\\
\dfrac{x}{x}&=1
\end{align}$

$\dfrac{7}{x}$ doesn't have common factors so it has to stay as it is.

In conclusion, this is the result of dividing the polynomials:

$5x+1+\dfrac{7}{x}$

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
We can perform the division using polynomial long division:

$\begin{array}{r}
5x+1
\\
x|\overline{5x^2+x+7}
\\
\mathllap{-(}\underline{5x^2\phantom{+x+7}\rlap )}
\\
x+7
\\
\mathllap{-(}\underline{x\phantom{+7}\rlap )}
\\
7
\end{array}$

We get that the quotient is $5x+1$ and the remainder is $7$, and therefore:

$\dfrac{5x^2+x+7}{x}=5x+1+\dfrac{7}{x}$
